text:
Arjun (vendor ops): Heads up 90 Tejas Labs (IN) emailed asking Redwood to gross-up their invoice by 10% TDS. They say Indian law will treat the payment as royalty and want to receive the net agreed amount.
Priya (tax): What's the vendor's legal form? Are they an Indian resident? If they are resident, typically no treaty relief needed; if non-resident, TDS may apply unless we get TRC + Form 10F.
Marcus (acct exec): Contract doesn't mention gross-up. They attached an email from their CA saying we must gross-up if we pay from an offshore entity. They provided PAN: AAAAA1111A and a GSTIN 27AAAAA1111A1Z5.
TaxBot: Quick tip: For treaty relief under India DTAA, vendor should provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from their tax authority plus Form 10F. Without TRC+10F, standard domestic TDS applies.
Hannah (payments): Policy: we do NOT gross-up unless legal/tax sign-off. I'll place a hold: "DO NOT GROSS-UP" and stop payment until resolved.
Arjun (vendor ops): Vendor insists their ERP can't create gross-up lines; they ask Redwood to pay a higher gross amount instead. They claim payment will be sent from Redwood NL, triggering non-resident rules.
Priya (tax): Ask vendor to send: 1) certified TRC (Sourced from Indian tax authority if they claim residency elsewhere) OR 2) if they are Indian resident, explain why they claim WHT applies. Also request the tax advisor memo referencing the specific ITA provision.
Marcus (acct exec): Customer wants month-end. Can we offer provisional payment and then true-up once docs arrive? That risks us overpaying.
Hannah (payments): We can offer two options: (A) vendor reissues invoice grossed-up (they accept new gross total) OR (B) we pay net and withhold TDS per rules and provide TDS certificates (Form 16A) so vendor can claim credit. Both need docs.
Arjun (vendor ops): Sent vendor the options and asked for TRC/10F if they're claiming treaty relief. Also asked them to confirm payer entity (NL vs IN vs US).
TaxBot: Reminder: save all tax docs to tax_evidence/2024/in_tejas_aaaaa1111a and capture payment routing evidence for audit.
Priya (tax): If payment originates from NL and they are non-resident, treaty relief requires TRC+10F. If vendor can't provide, we must withhold at the domestic rate (likely 10-30% depending on nature). We won't gross-up without signed amendment.
Marcus (acct exec): Update: vendor says they can get a TRC but it'll take 7-10 business days. They asked if we can start a partial payment.
Hannah (payments): Partial payment okay only if vendor signs an acknowledgement accepting the partial and agreeing to process any refund/adjustment once docs arrive. I'll mark AR ticket and hold remainder.
Arjun (vendor ops): Vendor uploaded a draft TRC (stamped PDF) and an email from their CA. Sending link: https://files.tejas.example/trc_draft.pdf
Priya (tax): Draft TRC not enough; need official TRC issued by tax authority plus completed Form 10F (signed). Also require PAN verification and bank details to match their legal name.
TaxBot: Note: Form 10F fields include nature of income, period of residence, tax identification number. Keep copy in archive.
Hannah (payments): Holding. Flag: "HOLD - TDS/RESIDENCY PEND TRC". No reissue until tax confirms.
Marcus (acct exec): I'll offer vendor the option to reissue grossed invoice + signed acceptance to speed payment, but legal must sign off.
Priya (tax): I'll review TRC when final arrives. If valid, we'll apply treaty rate and request Form 10F. If not, we withhold per Indian law and issue TDS certificate. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
